items.title: A released QFI is not reused, so a PDU session's 63rd QoS flow fails

labels.name: closed-loop-qos
labels.description: This label is to track the Dynamic Closed Loop QoS Feature of OAI Core Network

items.body:
## Summary

The SMF gives each new QoS flow of a PDU session a QFI from a per-session generator, and frees the QFI when the flow is removed. The generator never hands a freed value out again until its 8-bit counter wraps.

So the QFIs a session uses climb 2, 3, 4, … with every flow ever added, whether or not the earlier ones are still in use. At 64 the SMF reports "QFI pool exhausted" and rejects the change.

An AF that adds and removes one flow on a UE therefore succeeds 62 times, then fails about 190 times in a row, until the counter wraps. All that time only the default flow is active.

## Root cause (SMF develop b2374073)

- **Each PDU session's graph has one generator,** `oai::utils::uint_generator<uint8_t> qfi_generator` (`src/smf_app/smf_pfcp_association.hpp:241`).
  - `upf_graph::generate_qfi()` returns `qfi_generator.get_uid()` (`smf_pfcp_association.cpp:1536-1538`).
  - `upf_graph::release_qfi()` calls `qfi_generator.free_uid()` (`:1541-1542`).
- **The SMF does free the QFI of a removed flow.** `session_update_sm_context_procedure::commit_staged_flow_removals()` calls `release_qfi()` once the UPF has accepted the removal, with the comment "Frees the QFI for reuse" (`smf_procedure.cpp:2103-2137`).
- **The generator does not reuse what is freed.** In common-src (`utils/uint_generator.hpp`, read at 421b315f; the SMF pins 085dce7, and the class has only changed formatting since it was added):

  ```cpp
  // uint_generator.hpp:77-97, abridged
  UINT get_uid() {
    UINT uid = ++uid_generator;            // the counter only counts up
    while (true) {
      if (uid_generated.count(uid) == 0) { uid_generated.insert(uid); return uid; }
      uid = ++uid_generator;               // skips values still in use
    }
  }
  void free_uid(UINT uid) { uid_generated.erase(uid); }   // the counter is not touched
  ```

  `free_uid()` only takes the value out of the in-use set, and `get_uid()` always moves on from the last value it gave. A freed value comes back only after the counter wraps, which for `uint8_t` is after 256 values.
- **Above 63 the SMF gives up.** A QFI is 6 bits (TS 29.244 V17.10.0 §8.2.89), and the SMF checks the range:

  ```cpp
  // smf_context.cpp:2834-2843, abridged
  qfi_to_use = session_graph->generate_qfi();
  if (qfi_to_use == 0 || qfi_to_use > 63) {
    if (qfi_to_use != 0) session_graph->release_qfi(qfi_to_use);  // out of range
    Logger::smf_app().error("QFI pool exhausted, cannot add flow for rule '%s'", ...);
  ```

  Each failed attempt still moves the counter on by one. So the 63rd flow ever added to a session fails, and so do the 191 attempts after it, while the counter runs through 64–255.
  - Value 0, at the wrap, is rejected but not released. It then stays in the in-use set for the session's lifetime.
  - From then on the counter starts again at 1, skipping the default flow's QFI, and the freed values are reused.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Any deployment with a PCF that takes AF requests (Npcf_PolicyAuthorization), for example oai-cn5g-fed PR 4's QoS tutorial A, and one UE with a PDU session.
2. Repeat 70 times: the AF creates an app session with one media component on the UE's flow (a GBR QoS reference), then deletes it.
3. Watch the QFI of each create in the PFCP Session Modification Requests (Create QER and Create PDR), and the SMF's log.

## Observed

- **One UE, create then delete, 10 times.** The creates got QFIs 2, 3, 4, …, 11. Each delete was accepted by the UPF and the QFI released.
- **29 UEs under the AF's load, each toggled between create and delete,** about 100 creates per UE by the end, on the UPF's simple switch, which answers every PFCP request in about 2 ms:

| Step (requests/s) | Creates | Answered `500` by the SMF |
|---|---|---|
| 2, 5, 10, 20 | 600 | 0 |
| 50 | 790 | 1 |
| 100 | 1,511 | **1,100** |

  - The SMF logged "QFI pool exhausted, cannot add flow for rule 'PA-QOS-…'" 1,944 times, then "Could not allocate a QFI for … PCC rule(s), reporting them as inactive".
  - The PCF logged "RULE_PERMANENT_ERROR" for each.
  - No PFCP request followed: the UPF was not involved.
  - The failures began as each UE passed about 62 creates, not at any request rate.

## Expected

A released QFI can be used again for the session's next QoS flow. A session should only run out of QFIs when 63 flows are active at once.

## Suggested fix

Let the QFI counter wrap within the QFI's own range, 1–63, instead of 1–255:
- **Give `upf_graph` a small bounded allocator.** For example, a 64-bit mask of the QFIs in use and the last QFI handed out.
  - `generate_qfi()` steps from the last QFI to the next free one, going from 63 back to 1, and returns 0 only after a full lap finds all 63 in use. `release_qfi()` clears the bit.
  - The default flow's QFI stays set for the session's lifetime.
  - "QFI pool exhausted" then means what it says.
- **Prefer this to the lowest free QFI.** Wrapping keeps the generator's present order, so a released QFI is the last to come back rather than the first. That gives the RAN and the UE the most time to let go of the old flow.
  - On develop a removal is not signalled to them at all (the SMF builds no N2 Modify Request for a PCF-initiated removal). So a QFI reused at once could find the old flow still set up under it at the gNB and the UE.
- **Do not change `uint_generator` itself.** TEIDs, SEIDs and the PDR, FAR, QER and URR IDs use it too. There, not handing a just-freed value out at once can be intended: a packet still in flight for a deleted TEID should not match a new session. A QFI only has to be unique among a session's active flows (TS 23.501 V17.15.0 §5.7.1.1), and its range is too small for a counter.
- **Tests:** add and remove one flow 200 times on a session and expect every QFI to be in 2–63 and every add to succeed. With 63 flows active, the next add fails and succeeds again after one removal.

items.title: SMF: IP address allocation failure in PDU session establishment may accumulate SMF PDU session contexts
items.body:
### Summary

The SMF registers an `smf_pdu_session` into the SM context before it has an IP address for it.
When address allocation then fails, `smf_context::handle_pdu_session_create_sm_context_request()` sends a PDU Session Establishment Reject and returns without calling the release API, `smf_context::remove_pdu_session()`. The session object stays live in `smf_context::pdu_sessions` for a PDU session the UE was already told had failed.

The only cleanup that touches it is collision handling for a *new* INITIAL_REQUEST on the same identity, which is not a rollback of the failed request. The PoC confirms one surviving object per PDU session identity and zero releases on the error path.

### Details

Source analysis on `v2.2.1` (April 2026), SMF commit `53af440`.

**1. The session is registered before the address is allocated**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L857-L871

`smf_context::add_pdu_session()` inserts it into `pdu_sessions`, keyed by PDU session identity. From here `find_pdu_session()` and every consumer of the SM context sees it.

**2. The failure point**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L996-L1010

Four more early returns in the same function follow the registration and have the same shape: `:978` (IPv4v6, pool exhausted), `:1027` and `:1042` (PDU session type not supported), `:1059` (unknown type).

**3. The release API is never reached.**

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_context.cpp#L3447-L3452

`smf_context::remove_pdu_session()` has one call site outside the context class:

https://github.com/openairinterface/oai-cn5g-smf/blob/53af440450d2ece3a3908ba9f87febc4187d232c/src/smf_app/smf_app.cpp#L1073-L1080

That is collision handling — it fires when a new INITIAL_REQUEST arrives for an identity that already has a session and an SCID mapping. It is not cleanup for a request that failed, and a survivor that never reached SCID creation is not covered by it. Nothing unwinds the registration on the reject path itself.

### PoC

The `default` DNN pool was set to a `/30` so address allocation runs out. One UE then attempts several PDU sessions. No source change.

```
contexts registered ("PDU Session Id (N) has been added successfully") : 33
rejects             ("Could not get PAA ... for DNN default")          : 33
contexts removed    (remove_pdu_session debug line)                    : 31
net still in the map                                                   :  2
```

Counts of SMF log lines over one run, from a freshly started SMF.

- **The error path never releases.** Every registration is followed by a reject, and no removal ever follows one. All 33 registrations leaked at the point of failure.
- **The removals come from the next request, not from the failure.** Each removal in the log is preceded by a fresh INITIAL_REQUEST and the `PDU Session already existed` warning from `smf_app.cpp:1077` — the collision cleanup. The UE retransmitted on the same identity, and that retransmission is what cleared the previous object.
- **What is left over stays.** Once the requests stop, the last object on each identity has nothing to clear it and remains in `pdu_sessions` until the `smf_context` is destroyed. The run used identities 1 and 2 and ended with 2 objects still there.

A single attempt, with no removal between registration and reject:

```
01:06:18.674 [smf_app][info]    Add PDU Session with Id 2
01:06:18.675 [smf_app][debug]   PDU Session Id (2) has been added successfully
01:06:18.675 [smf_app][warning] Could not get PAA PDU_SESSION_TYPE_E_IPV4 for DNN default
01:06:18.675 [smf_n1 ][info]    Create N1 SM Container, PDU Session Establishment Reject
```

### Impact


Address pool exhaustion needs no unusual configuration to reach: a busy DNN, a pool sized for fewer subscribers than attach, or addresses held by sessions that were never released all end at the same get_free_paa() failure. While that lasts, every PDU session attempt leaves an object behind.

The object is usually short-lived, because the UE's own retransmission clears it. The collision cleanup at smf_app.cpp:1073 runs before the handler, so the next INITIAL_REQUEST on that identity removes the previous object and the handler builds a fresh one. That is what the PoC shows: 33 registrations against 33 rejects, with 31 removals all attributable to a following request.

What is not guaranteed is that anything ever clears it. Nothing in the failure path does, and the collision cleanup only runs if another INITIAL_REQUEST arrives on the same identity. When the UE gives up, or moves to a different identity, the object stays in pdu_sessions until the smf_context is destroyed. The run ended with 2 such objects, one per identity used.

Memory growth is bounded by the PDU session identity space per UE, and everything is freed with the smf_context.
